chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Al-Numan, from one of our companions, who said:

I complained to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the pain, so he said: 'When you lie down on your bed, eat two pieces of sugar.' He said: 'So I did it, and I was cured. And I informed one of the physicians of it, and he was the most renowned of the people of our city. He said: 'From where did Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) know this? This is from the treasures of our knowledge. Indeed, he is the owner of books; it is fitting that he found it in one of his books.'
ai.seo_question: What medical remedy did Imam Al-Sadiq prescribe for pain, and how did contemporary scholars view the source of his medical knowledge?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Imam’s practical medical wisdom, where consuming sugar before sleep cured the narrator’s ailment. A prominent physician, known for his expertise, attributes this specific remedy to the Imam’s extensive library, affirming that such knowledge is part of the 'treasures of their knowledge' (*makhzan 'ilminā*). This underscores the Shia belief in the Imam’s comprehensive mastery of both spiritual and worldly sciences, including medicine.

en.hubeali: H 14833 – From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al-Hassan Bin Ali Bin Al-No’man, from one of our companions who said:

I complained to Abu Abdullahasws of the aches, so heasws said: ‘When you go to your bed, take two (pieces) of sugar’. So he said, ‘I did it. So I was free from it, and I informed one of the doctors who was a renowned one of our city. He said, ‘From where did Abu Abdullahasws understand this? This is from the treasures of our knowledge. But heasws is the owner of Books. He probably got it from one of hisasws Books’.
